claims.source: The fourth class, which accounts for a relatively small proportion of mutant vesicles (4.9%), contains various cellular organelles, for instance mitochondria (Figure 2Q).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy analysis and quantification of vesicle types.

claims.claim: GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 in worm epidermal cells
claims.source: In worm epidermal cells, the GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) but not with mCherry::RAB-7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the early endosomal localization of USP-50/USP8 (Mizuno et al., 2005; Row et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is not co-localized with mCherry::RAB-7 in worm epidermal cells
claims.source: In worm epidermal cells, the GFP-tagged USP-50 protein is co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) but not with mCherry::RAB-7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the early endosomal localization of USP-50/USP8 (Mizuno et al., 2005; Row et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: The early endosome localization of USP-50 is not dependent on its deubiquitination activity
claims.source: When we mutated C492 to Alanine, we found that the GFP-tagged USP-50(C492A) protein is still co-localized with mCherry::RAB-5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). Thus, the EE localization of USP-50 is not dependent on its deubiquitination activity.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) showing that the catalytically inactive mutant still localizes to early endosomes.

claims.claim: The C492A mutation has a dominant-negative effect on USP-50 function
claims.source: Meanwhile, the mCherry::RAB-5 signal is strongly enhanced by the overexpression of USP-50(C492A) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the C492A mutation may have a dominant-negative effect on USP-50 function.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that overexpression of the catalytically inactive mutant enhances RAB-5 signal, suggesting it interferes with normal USP-50 function.

claims.claim: USP8-mEGFP co-localizes well with the early endosome marker mScarlet-I-EEA1
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3, USP8-mEGFP co-localizes well with the EE marker mScarlet-I-EEA1 (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3A).

claims.claim: Late endosome or lysosome markers have little overlap with the USP8-mEGFP signal
claims.source: In contrast, LE or lysosome markers, including mScarlet-I-Rab7a and Lamp1-mScarlet-I, have little overlap with the USP8-mEGFP signal (Figure 3B and C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3B and C) showing minimal overlap.

claims.claim: USP8-mEGFP forms individual spots located on one side of enlarged endosomes caused by Rab5c-Q80L overexpression
claims.source: Constitutively activated Rab5 GTPase (Rab5c-Q80L) causes enlarged EEs (Stenmark et al., 1994; Wegner et al., 2010). Instead of being evenly distributed, USP8-mEGFP formed individual spots located on one side of the enlarged endosomes (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 3D) showing the asymmetric distribution of USP8 on enlarged endosomes.

claims.claim: USP8-mEGFP dots are located at subdomains of early endosomes as shown by structured illumination microscopy
claims.source: We further analyzed the sub-organelle distribution of USP8 using structured illumination microscopy (SIM). Consistent with what we observed in enlarged EEs caused by Rab5c-Q80L overexpression, the USP8-mEGFP dots indeed located at subdomains of EEs (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by structured illumination microscopy images (Figure 3E) showing sub-organelle localization.

claims.claim: USP8-mEGFP is recruited to nascent mScarlet-I-Rab5c-positive vesicles
claims.source: We found that USP8-mEGFP was recruited to these nascent mScarlet-I-Rab5c-positive vesicles which appeared around the bottom surface of the cells (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy images (Figure 3F) showing dynamic recruitment.

claims.claim: USP-50 can bind to RABX-5
claims.source: By searching the putative USP-50-binding partners, we found that USP-50 can bind to RABX-5, the worm homolog of Rabex5 protein (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 4A and B).

claims.claim: The C-terminal coiled-coil and C-terminal proline-rich domains of RABX-5 are sufficient for interaction with USP-50
claims.source: In general, the C-terminal coiled-coil (CC) and the C-terminal proline-rich (PR) domains are sufficient for RABX-5 to interact with USP-50.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests with truncation mutants (Figure 4D).

claims.claim: The N-terminal region of RABX-5 including A20-zinc finger domain, motif interacting with ubiquitin, membrane-binding motif, and helical bundle domain can mediate USP-50 binding
claims.source: Meanwhile, the N-terminal region, including an A20-zinc finger domain (ZF), a motif interacting with ubiquitin (U), the membrane-binding motif (MB), and the downstream helical bundle domain (HB) of RABX-5 could also mediate USP-50 binding.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests with truncation mutants (Figure 4D).

claims.claim: Including the Vps9 domain enhances the molecular interaction between RABX-5 and USP-50
claims.source: Further including Vps9 domain enhances the molecular interaction between RABX-5 and USP-50 (Figure 4C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation tests (Figure 4D) showing enhanced binding with Vps9 domain inclusion.

claims.claim: rabx-5 is required for the endosomal localization of USP-50
claims.source: In rabx-5(null) mutant animals, the punctate USP-50::GFP signal becomes diffusely distributed (Figure 4F and G). Thus, rabx-5 is required for the endosomal localization of USP-50.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 4F and G) showing loss of punctate USP-50 localization in rabx-5(null) mutants.

claims.claim: Early endosomes labeled with 2xFYVE are indistinguishable from wild-type in rabx-5(null) mutant animals
claims.source: In rabx-5(null) mutant animals, EEs labeled with 2xFYVE are indistinguishable from those in wild-type controls (Figure 4H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 4H and I).

claims.claim: rabx-5(null) mutation suppresses the enlarged early endosome phenotype of usp-50(xd413)
claims.source: Furthermore, when rabx-5(null) was introduced into usp-50(xd413) mutant backgrounds, the enlarged EE phenotype of usp-50(xd413) was efficiently suppressed (Figure 4H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 4H and I) showing suppression of the phenotype.

claims.claim: USP-50 likely exerts its regulatory effects on early endosome size through RABX-5
claims.source: These findings suggest that USP-50 likely exerts its regulatory effects on EE size through RABX-5.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic suppression experiments showing that loss of rabx-5 suppresses the usp-50 phenotype.

claims.claim: The RABX-5::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: In wild-type animals, the fluorescence signal of RABX-5::GFP in hyp7 is rather dim (Figure 5A). When usp-50 is mutated, the RABX-5::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 5A and B) showing enhanced RABX-5 signal in mutants.

claims.claim: USP8-KO causes a significant increase in the number of enlarged endosomes in Rabex5-mEGFP+/+ SUM159 cells
claims.source: USP8-KO also caused a significant increase in the number of enlarged endosomes in Rabex5-mEGFP+/+ SUM159 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C and E).

claims.claim: Rabex5-mEGFP signals are enriched and co-localized well with the mScarlet-I-Rab5c signal on enlarged endosomes
claims.source: Rabex5-mEGFP signals were enriched and co-localized well with the mScarlet-I-Rab5c signal on the enlarged endosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: The enlarged early endosomes in USP8-KO cells are coated with both Rabex5 and EEA1
claims.source: Antibody staining of endogenous EEA1 further showed that the enlarged EEs in USP8-KO cells were coated with both Rabex5 and EEA1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy images (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claims.claim: GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: Indeed, in usp-50 mutants, the GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C) and the proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is also increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).

claims.claim: The proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is increased in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: Indeed, in usp-50 mutants, the GFP::RAB-5 KI-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C) and the proportion of membrane-associated GFP::RAB-5 KI is also increased (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).

claims.claim: Loss of usp-50 leads to more activated RAB-5 in vivo
claims.source: We utilized EEA1-NT (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E) to show that loss of usp-50 indeed led to more activated RAB-5 in vivo (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down assays (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F) using the RAB-5 effector EEA1-NT.

claims.claim: The total RAB-5 protein level is increased by usp-50 mutation
claims.source: In addition, the total RAB-5 protein level is increased by usp-50 mutation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H), which implies that RAB-5 activation may stabilize RAB-5 protein.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H).

claims.claim: Early endosomes labeled by Rab5 are significantly enlarged in USP8-KD SUM159 cells
claims.source: To explore the relationship between Rab5 and USP8 in SUM159 cells, we knocked down the expression of USP8 by siRNA (USP8-KD) in the clonal genome-edited EGFP-Rab5c+/+ cells. We found that EEs, labeled by Rab5, are significantly enlarged (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J).

claims.claim: USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes
claims.source: Taken together, these results indicate that USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes, and subsequently diminish Rab5 signaling.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing enhanced RABX-5 signal and increased Rab5 activity in usp-50 mutants.

claims.claim: The enzyme-inactive USP-50(C492A) cannot rescue the enhanced endosomal RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutant animals
claims.source: The enzyme-inactive USP-50(C492A) cannot rescue the enhanced endosomal RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutant animals (Figure 5C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images (Figure 5C and D) showing lack of rescue by the catalytically inactive mutant.

claims.claim: USP-50 acts through its deubiquitination activity to dissociate RABX-5 from endosomes
claims.source: This suggests that USP-50 acts through its deubiquitination activity to dissociate RABX-5 from endosomes.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the catalytically inactive mutant cannot rescue the phenotype.

claims.claim: The K88 and K323 residues of RABX-5 are modified by ubiquitin in vivo
claims.source: We found that the K88 and K323 residues of RABX-5 are modified by ubiquitin in vivo (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ubiquitination proteomics analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).

claims.claim: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif of RABX-5
claims.source: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif, while K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the domain structure diagram (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).

claims.claim: K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5
claims.source: K88 is located in the membrane-binding motif, while K323 resides in the conserved Vps9 domain of RABX-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the domain structure diagram (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).

claims.claim: The RABX-5(K88R)::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: When usp-50 is mutated, the RABX-5(K88R)::GFP KI signal is greatly enhanced and displays an apparent punctate pattern (Figure 5F and I), which is similar to what we observed with the wild-type RABX-5::GFP KI line.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 5F and I).

claims.claim: The signal from RABX-5(K323A)::GFP KI remains dim in both wild-type and usp-50 mutant animals
claims.source: In contrast, when K323 is mutated, the signal from RABX-5(K323A)::GFP KI remains dim in both wild-type and usp-50 mutant animals (Figure 5G–I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 5G–I).

claims.claim: USP-50 cannot regulate the endosomal localization of RABX-5 when K323 is mutated
claims.source: These observations suggest that USP-50 cannot regulate the endosomal localization of RABX-5 when K323 is mutated.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that K323R mutation prevents the enhancement of RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutants.

claims.claim: The rabx-5(K323R) mutation suppresses both the enlarged early endosome and diminished late endosome phenotypes of usp-50
claims.source: Furthermore, the rabx-5(K323R) mutation successfully suppressed both the enlarged EE and diminished LE phenotypes of usp-50 (Figure 5J–M).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 5J–M) showing suppression of both phenotypes.

claims.claim: USP-50 recruitment to early endosomes relies on RABX-5
claims.source: Taken together, USP-50 recruitment to EEs relies on RABX-5, and through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from EEs, thereby terminating Rab5 signaling to promote endosome maturation.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the observation that USP-50 localization is lost in rabx-5(null) mutants.

claims.claim: Through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from early endosomes
claims.source: Taken together, USP-50 recruitment to EEs relies on RABX-5, and through its deubiquitination action on the Vps9 domain of RABX-5, USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from EEs, thereby terminating Rab5 signaling to promote endosome maturation.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the K323R mutation experiments showing that this ubiquitination site is critical for USP-50 function.

claims.claim: The GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished in rabx-5(null) mutants
claims.source: In the absence of RABX-5 (rabx-5 null), the GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished (Figure 6A, B, and D) and the LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are also reduced (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6A, B, and D).

claims.claim: The LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are reduced in rabx-5(null) mutants
claims.source: In the absence of RABX-5 (rabx-5 null), the GFP::SAND-1 puncta are diminished (Figure 6A, B, and D) and the LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosome structures are also reduced (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6E and F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: The punctate distribution of GFP::SAND-1 is lost in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: Intriguingly, when we introduced the GFP::SAND-1 marker into usp-50 mutants, we found that the punctate distribution of GFP::SAND-1 is lost (Figure 6A, C, and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6A, C, and D).

claims.claim: mEGFP-tagged endogenous Mon1a is localized on both Rab5-positive early endosomes and Rab7-positive late endosomes
claims.source: In SUM159 cells, mEGFP-tagged endogenous Mon1a (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) is localized on both Rab5-positive EEs and Rab7-positive LEs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).

claims.claim: Endogenous Mon1b is more localized on late endosomes
claims.source: In contrast, endogenous Mon1b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E) is more localized on LEs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and G).

claims.claim: The number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a is greatly reduced when USP8 expression is knocked down
claims.source: When the expression of USP8 in the mEGFP-Mon1a+/+ or mEGFP-Mon1b+/+ cells was knocked down by siRNA, we found that the number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a or mEGFP-Mon1b was greatly reduced (Figure 6H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6H).

claims.claim: The number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1b is greatly reduced when USP8 expression is knocked down
claims.source: When the expression of USP8 in the mEGFP-Mon1a+/+ or mEGFP-Mon1b+/+ cells was knocked down by siRNA, we found that the number of vesicles positive for mEGFP-Mon1a or mEGFP-Mon1b was greatly reduced (Figure 6H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6I).

claims.claim: The function of USP8/USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 is evolutionarily conserved
claims.source: Taken together, these results indicate that the function of USP8/USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 is evolutionarily conserved.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the similar effects of USP8/USP-50 loss on Mon1/SAND-1 localization in both worms and mammalian cells.

claims.claim: Early endosomes are enlarged in sand-1 mutants
claims.source: We noticed that when sand-1 is mutated, the EEs are enlarged (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H) and LEs/lysosomes become smaller (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I), which is highly similar to usp-50 mutants.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).

claims.claim: Late endosomes/lysosomes become smaller in sand-1 mutants
claims.source: We noticed that when sand-1 is mutated, the EEs are enlarged (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H) and LEs/lysosomes become smaller (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I), which is highly similar to usp-50 mutants.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6M–O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).

claims.claim: The USP-50 protein is able to bind to SAND-1
claims.source: Furthermore, Co-IP (co-immunoprecipitation) experiments indicated that the USP-50 protein is able to bind to SAND-1 (Figure 6P), which is consistent with the role of USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 6P).

claims.claim: The punctate RAB-7 signal is greatly reduced by loss of function of sand-1
claims.source: Indeed, with the GFP::RAB-7 KI line, we found that the punctate RAB-7 signal was greatly reduced by loss of function of sand-1 (Figure 6Q and R).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6Q and R).

claims.claim: The punctate GFP::RAB-7 KI signal is reduced in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: In usp-50 mutants, the punctate GFP::RAB-7 KI signal is also reduced (Figure 6S and T).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6S and T).

claims.claim: Overexpression of wild-type rab-7 greatly suppresses the early endosome enlargement phenotype of usp-50 mutants
claims.source: Therefore, we overexpressed the wild-type rab-7 gene and found that the EE enlargement phenotype of usp-50 mutants was greatly suppressed (Figure 6U–X).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images and quantification (Figure 6U–X) showing suppression of the phenotype.

claims.claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from early endosomes
claims.source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claims.claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8 promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1
claims.source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claims.claim: The recruitment of USP-50/USP8 facilitates the maturation of endosomes
claims.source: In conclusion, we propose that the recruitment of USP-50/USP8, dependent on Rabex5, dissociates Rabex5 from EEs. Concurrently, this recruitment promotes the enrollment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, thereby facilitating the maturation of endosomes (Figure 6Y).
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the working model supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claims.claim: USP8 is important for the stability and ubiquitination status of various ESCRT components
claims.source: USP8 is important for the stability and ubiquitination status of various ESCRT components (Adoro et al., 2017; Crespo-Yàñez et al., 2018; Mathieu et al., 2022; Mizuno et al., 2006; Niendorf et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014a).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claims.claim: A large number of abnormal vesicular structures accumulate in usp-50 mutants
claims.source: By EM ultrastructural analysis, we found that a large number of abnormal vesicular structures accumulate in usp-50 mutants and a large portion of them contain various intraluminal structures (Figure 2L–Q).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy images (Figure 2L–Q).

claims.claim: The loss of USP-50 results in the upregulation of Rab5 signaling
claims.source: The loss of USP-50 results in the upregulation of Rab5 signaling, which may enhance the homophilic fusion of EEs.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased Rab5 levels and activity observed in usp-50 mutants.

claims.claim: The aberrantly enlarged vesicles in usp-50 mutants likely represent excessively enlarged early endosomes
claims.source: Given the substantial reduction in Rab7 levels and the marked diminution in lysosomal structures, it is likely that the aberrantly enlarged vesicles in usp-50 mutants represent excessively enlarged EEs.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the combination of reduced Rab7 levels, reduced lysosomes, and the presence of enlarged vesicles with ILV structures.

claims.claim: USP8 is a promising target in cancer therapy to overcome chemoresistance associated with RTK stabilization
claims.source: USP8 deubiquitinates numerous plasma membrane receptors, making this enzyme a promising target in cancer therapy to overcome chemoresistance associated with RTK stabilization (Byun et al., 2013; Islam et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Byun et al., 2013; Islam et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Gain-of-function mutations of USP8 have been found in microadenomas of patients with Cushing's disease
claims.source: Gain-of-function mutations of USP8 have been found in microadenomas of patients with Cushing's disease, a rare disease where the secretion of large amounts of adrenocorticotrophic hormone by pituitary corticotroph adenomas results in an excess of glucocorticoids and hypercortisolism, putatively due to defective EGFR sorting (Ma et al., 2015; Reincke et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ma et al., 2015; Reincke et al., 2015).

claims.claim: The spatiotemporal transition of small GTPase Rab5 to Rab7 is crucial for early-to-late endosome maturation
claims.source: The spatiotemporal transition of small GTPase Rab5 to Rab7 is crucial for early-to-late endosome maturation, yet the precise mechanism governing Rab5-to-Rab7 switching remains elusive.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field, as indicated by the context of the abstract.

claims.claim: USP8 is recruited to Rab5-positive carriers by Rabex5
claims.source: Here, we identified that USP8 is recruited to Rab5-positive carriers by Rabex5, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) for Rab5.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the main finding supported by multiple experiments in the study.

claims.claim: The recruitment of USP8 dissociates Rabex5 from early endosomes
claims.source: The recruitment of USP8 dissociates Rabex5 from early endosomes (EEs) and meanwhile promotes the recruitment of the Rab7 GEF SAND-1/Mon1.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the main finding supported by multiple experiments in the study.

claims.claim: The recruitment of USP8 promotes the recruitment of the Rab7 GEF SAND-1/Mon1
claims.source: The recruitment of USP8 dissociates Rabex5 from early endosomes (EEs) and meanwhile promotes the recruitment of the Rab7 GEF SAND-1/Mon1.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of the main finding supported by multiple experiments in the study.

claims.claim: In USP8-deficient cells, the level of active Rab5 is increased
claims.source: In USP8-deficient cells, the level of active Rab5 is increased, while the Rab7 signal is decreased.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of findings supported by pull-down assays and microscopy data.

claims.claim: In USP8-deficient cells, the Rab7 signal is decreased
claims.source: In USP8-deficient cells, the level of active Rab5 is increased, while the Rab7 signal is decreased.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of findings supported by microscopy data.

claims.claim: Enlarged early endosomes with abundant intraluminal vesicles accumulate in USP8-deficient cells
claims.source: As a result, enlarged EEs with abundant intraluminal vesicles accumulate and digestive lysosomes are rudimentary.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of findings supported by electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy data.

claims.claim: Digestive lysosomes are rudimentary in USP8-deficient cells
claims.source: As a result, enlarged EEs with abundant intraluminal vesicles accumulate and digestive lysosomes are rudimentary.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary of findings supported by microscopy data showing reduced lysosome size and volume.

claims.claim: Rab5 can be activated and recruited to early endosomes by its GEF, Rabex5
claims.source: Rab5, the Rab GTPase critical for EE formation and function, can be activated and recruited to EEs by its GEF, Rabex5 (Mattera and Bonifacino, 2008; Zhu et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mattera and Bonifacino, 2008; Zhu et al., 2007).

claims.claim: The GTP-bound active Rab5 recruits Rabaptin-5
claims.source: The GTP-bound active Rab5 recruits its effectors, for instance, Rabaptin-5. Rabaptin-5 in turn binds to Rabex5 via a coiled-coil region, resulting in a positive feedback loop of Rab5 activation on endosomal membranes (Zhang et al., 2014b).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Zhang et al., 2014b).

claims.claim: Rabaptin-5 binds to Rabex5 via a coiled-coil region, resulting in a positive feedback loop of Rab5 activation
claims.source: The GTP-bound active Rab5 recruits its effectors, for instance, Rabaptin-5. Rabaptin-5 in turn binds to Rabex5 via a coiled-coil region, resulting in a positive feedback loop of Rab5 activation on endosomal membranes (Zhang et al., 2014b).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Zhang et al., 2014b).

claims.claim: Isolated Rabex5 has relatively low GEF activity in vitro
claims.source: Isolated Rabex5 appears to have relatively low GEF activity in vitro (Delprato and Lambright, 2007) and binding of Rabaptin-5 to Rabex5 causes a rearrangement in the Rabex5 C-terminus and subsequently enhances nucleotide exchange of Rab5 (Horiuchi et al., 1997; Lauer et al., 2019; Lippé et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2014b).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Delprato and Lambright, 2007).

claims.claim: Binding of Rabaptin-5 to Rabex5 enhances nucleotide exchange of Rab5
claims.source: Isolated Rabex5 appears to have relatively low GEF activity in vitro (Delprato and Lambright, 2007) and binding of Rabaptin-5 to Rabex5 causes a rearrangement in the Rabex5 C-terminus and subsequently enhances nucleotide exchange of Rab5 (Horiuchi et al., 1997; Lauer et al., 2019; Lippé et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2014b).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Horiuchi et al., 1997; Lauer et al., 2019; Lippé et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2014b).

claims.claim: Autoinhibition serves as a key regulatory mechanism in controlling GEF activity
claims.source: Thus, autoinhibition likely serves as a key regulatory mechanism in controlling GEF activity.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Rabex5 has low activity in isolation but is activated by Rabaptin-5 binding.

claims.claim: Rab5 recruits the Mon1-Ccz1 complex
claims.source: Rab5 effectors also include the Rab7 GEF Mon1-Ccz1 complex. Rab7 activation by Mon1-Ccz1 complex is essential for the biogenesis and positioning of late endosomes (LEs) and lysosomes, and for the fusion of endosomes and autophagosomes with lysosomes.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claims.claim: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex is a heterodimer in yeast
claims.source: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex is a heterodimer in yeast, and a heterotrimer in metazoan cells (Dehnen et al., 2020; Vaites et al., 2018; van den Boomen et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Dehnen et al., 2020; Vaites et al., 2018; van den Boomen et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2002).

claims.claim: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex is a heterotrimer in metazoan cells
claims.source: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex is a heterodimer in yeast, and a heterotrimer in metazoan cells (Dehnen et al., 2020; Vaites et al., 2018; van den Boomen et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Dehnen et al., 2020; Vaites et al., 2018; van den Boomen et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2002).

claims.claim: The activation of Mon1-Ccz1 is dependent on Rab5 interaction
claims.source: The activation of Mon1-Ccz1 is depended on Rab5 interaction (Borchers et al., 2023; Langemeyer et al., 2020) and Mon1 also coordinates endosome maturation together with the Rab5 GAP TBC1D18 (Hiragi et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Borchers et al., 2023; Langemeyer et al., 2020).

claims.claim: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex is able to interact with Rabex5
claims.source: Additionally, the Mon1-Ccz1 complex is able to interact with Rabex5 (Poteryaev et al., 2010), causing dissociation of Rabex5 from the membrane, which probably terminates the positive feedback loop of Rab5 activation and then promotes the recruitment and activation of Rab7 on endosomes (Nordmann et al., 2010; Poteryaev et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Poteryaev et al., 2010).

claims.claim: The Mon1-Ccz1 complex causes dissociation of Rabex5 from the membrane
claims.source: Additionally, the Mon1-Ccz1 complex is able to interact with Rabex5 (Poteryaev et al., 2010), causing dissociation of Rabex5 from the membrane, which probably terminates the positive feedback loop of Rab5 activation and then promotes the recruitment and activation of Rab7 on endosomes (Nordmann et al., 2010; Poteryaev et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Nordmann et al., 2010; Poteryaev et al., 2010).

claims.claim: USP8 plays a prominent role in the regulation of endosomal sorting of a wide range of transmembrane receptors
claims.source: The deubiquitinating enzyme (DUB) USP8 belongs to the ubiquitin-specific protease (USP) family and plays a prominent role in the regulation of endosomal sorting of a wide range of transmembrane receptors (Dufner and Knobeloch, 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Dufner and Knobeloch, 2019).

claims.claim: USP8 stabilizes the ESCRT-0 complex by binding to STAM and Hrs
claims.source: By binding to STAM and Hrs, USP8 stabilizes the ESCRT-0 complex, which is the crucial element directing ubiquitinated substrates toward MVB/lysosome-mediated degradation (Mizuno et al., 2006; Row et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mizuno et al., 2006; Row et al., 2006).

claims.claim: In the absence of USP8, EGFR is abnormally accumulated in early endosomes
claims.source: In the absence of USP8, EGFR is abnormally accumulated in EEs (Alwan and van Leeuwen, 2007; Row et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Alwan and van Leeuwen, 2007; Row et al., 2006).

claims.claim: The endocytic trafficking of the Frizzled receptor is affected by usp8 deficiency
claims.source: Additionally, the endocytic trafficking of the Frizzled receptor, Smooth, as well as key components of the Wnt and Hedgehog pathways is also affected by usp8 deficiency (Ali et al., 2013; Berlin et al., 2010a; Berlin et al., 2010b; Crespo-Yàñez et al., 2018; Jacomin et al., 2015; MacDonald et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ali et al., 2013; Berlin et al., 2010a; Berlin et al., 2010b; Crespo-Yàñez et al., 2018; Jacomin et al., 2015; MacDonald et al., 2014).

claims.claim: The impact of USP8 on protein stability is highly variable and sometimes controversial
claims.source: Noticeably, however, the impact of USP8 on protein stability is highly variable and sometimes controversial (Berlin et al., 2010b; Mizuno et al., 2005; Niendorf et al., 2007; Row et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies showing conflicting results (Berlin et al., 2010b; Mizuno et al., 2005; Niendorf et al., 2007; Row et al., 2006).

claims.claim: USP8 has recently arisen as a promising therapeutic target in pathological contexts associated with USP8 overexpression or gain-of-function variants
claims.source: USP8 has recently arisen as a promising therapeutic target in at least two distinct pathological contexts associated with USP8 overexpression or gain-of-function variants (Dufner and Knobeloch, 2019; Li et al., 2024; Reincke et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Dufner and Knobeloch, 2019; Li et al., 2024; Reincke et al., 2015).

results.result: Loss of usp-50 function leads to reduced lysosome size in C. elegans, with temporal differences between alleles, but does not affect de novo lysosome assembly as indicated by proper NUC-1 targeting.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 are well-supported by microscopy images and quantification showing reduced lysosome size in usp-50 mutants (Figure 1B-D), temporal phenotype differences between alleles (Figure 1C-D), and proper co-localization of NUC-1 with LAAT-1 (Figure 1E-F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A). The data consistently demonstrate the lysosomal phenotype without affecting lysosome biogenesis.

results.result: usp-50 encodes the C. elegans homolog of yeast Doa4p and human USP8/UBPY, with mutations in both alleles occurring in the UCH domain (G541A in xd413 and A523V in gk632973).
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C6 are supported by citations establishing homology relationships and molecular characterization of the mutations. The identification of specific amino acid substitutions in the UCH domain provides clear molecular basis for the observed phenotypes.

results.result: The punctate signals of ESCRT-0 components HGRS-1::GFP and STAM-1 are greatly reduced in usp-50 mutants, consistent with USP8's role in stabilizing the ESCRT-0 complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C8 are well-supported by microscopy images (Figure 1G-H) and quantification (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) showing reduced ESCRT-0 component signals. The findings are consistent with cited literature on USP8 function in ESCRT-0 stabilization.

results.result: Early endosomes are significantly enlarged in usp-50 mutants with increased individual vesicle size but similar total volume compared to wild-type, and these enlarged EEs remain distinct from lysosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C11 are supported by quantification data (Figure 2B) showing increased individual EE size with unchanged total volume, and co-localization analysis (Figure 2C-D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) demonstrating that enlarged EEs do not overlap with lysosome markers. The data suggest increased homotypic fusion of EEs.

results.result: The enlarged early endosome phenotype in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by both worm usp-50 and human USP8, demonstrating evolutionary conservation of USP-50/USP8 function.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C14 are well-supported by rescue experiments (Figure 2G, J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) showing that both worm and human orthologs can restore normal EE size. The cross-species rescue provides strong evidence for functional conservation.

results.result: USP8 depletion causes early endosome enlargement in human breast cancer SUM159 cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C15 is supported by microscopy and quantification (Figure 2K) showing enlarged EEs in USP8-KO SUM159 cells expressing EGFP-2xFYVE. This extends the findings from C. elegans to mammalian cells.

results.result: Transmission electron microscopy reveals accumulation of abnormal large vesicles with various intraluminal contents in usp-50(xd413) mutants, classified into four categories based on their contents.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C20 and C77 are supported by electron microscopy images (Figure 2L-Q) and quantification (Figure 2M) showing abnormal vesicles with specific percentages for each category. The detailed ultrastructural analysis provides strong evidence for the vesicular phenotype.

results.result: USP-50 localizes to early endosomes (co-localizing with RAB-5 but not RAB-7) in a manner independent of its deubiquitination activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C23 are supported by co-localization microscopy (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C) showing USP-50::GFP co-localizes with RAB-5 but not RAB-7, and that the catalytically inactive C492A mutant retains EE localization. The data clearly demonstrate early endosomal localization independent of enzymatic activity.

results.result: The C492A mutation has a dominant-negative effect on USP-50 function.
results.evaluation: Claim C24 is inferred from enhanced RAB-5 signal upon C492A overexpression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), but the evidence is limited to this single observation. Additional experiments would be needed to definitively establish a dominant-negative mechanism versus other possible explanations for the enhanced signal.

results.result: In mammalian cells, USP8-mEGFP co-localizes well with early endosome marker EEA1 but shows little overlap with late endosome or lysosome markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C26 are supported by co-localization microscopy images (Figure 3A-C) in genome-edited SUM159 cells showing strong overlap with EEA1 and minimal overlap with Rab7a and Lamp1. This confirms early endosomal localization in mammalian cells.

results.result: USP8 forms individual spots at subdomains of early endosomes and is dynamically recruited to nascent Rab5-positive vesicles.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C29 are supported by multiple imaging approaches including conventional microscopy (Figure 3D), structured illumination microscopy (Figure 3E), and time-lapse imaging (Figure 3F-H) showing asymmetric USP8 distribution on enlarged endosomes and dynamic recruitment to nascent Rab5-positive carriers. The multi-modal imaging provides strong evidence for dynamic USP8 localization.

results.result: USP-50 binds to RABX-5 through multiple domains, with the C-terminal coiled-coil and proline-rich domains being sufficient for interaction, and the Vps9 domain enhancing binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C33 are supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 4A-B) and systematic domain mapping using truncation mutants (Figure 4C-D). The comprehensive domain analysis provides clear evidence for the molecular interaction and identifies key binding regions.

results.result: RABX-5 is required for endosomal localization of USP-50, and loss of rabx-5 suppresses the enlarged early endosome phenotype of usp-50 mutants, indicating USP-50 acts through RABX-5.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C37 are well-supported by microscopy showing loss of punctate USP-50 localization in rabx-5(null) mutants (Figure 4F-G) and genetic suppression experiments (Figure 4H-I) demonstrating that rabx-5(null) rescues the usp-50 EE phenotype. The genetic epistasis analysis provides strong evidence for the pathway relationship.

results.result: RABX-5/Rabex5 signal is greatly enhanced on endosomes in usp-50/USP8 mutants, with enlarged endosomes containing both Rabex5 and EEA1.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41 are supported by microscopy images and quantification in both C. elegans (Figure 5A-B) and mammalian cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-E) showing enhanced Rabex5 signal and co-localization with Rab5 and EEA1 on enlarged endosomes. The conservation across species strengthens the findings.

results.result: Loss of usp-50/USP8 leads to increased Rab5 levels, increased membrane-associated Rab5, increased activated Rab5, and upregulation of Rab5 signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C46 and C78 are supported by multiple lines of evidence including microscopy showing enlarged RAB-5-positive vesicles (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C), quantification of membrane-associated RAB-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D), pull-down assays with EEA1-NT showing increased active RAB-5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F), and western blots showing increased total RAB-5 levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 2G-H). The comprehensive analysis provides strong evidence for upregulated Rab5 signaling.

results.result: USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes through its deubiquitination activity, as the catalytically inactive C492A mutant cannot rescue the enhanced RABX-5 signal.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C49 are supported by the failure of the C492A mutant to rescue enhanced RABX-5 signal (Figure 5C-D), combined with the enhanced RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutants. The requirement for catalytic activity provides strong evidence for a deubiquitination-dependent mechanism.

results.result: RABX-5 is ubiquitinated at K88 (in the membrane-binding motif) and K323 (in the Vps9 domain) in vivo.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C52 are supported by ubiquitination proteomics analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-B) identifying specific ubiquitination sites and their locations within RABX-5 domains. The mass spectrometry data provides direct evidence for these post-translational modifications.

results.result: USP-50 regulates RABX-5 endosomal localization through deubiquitination of K323 in the Vps9 domain, as the K323R mutation prevents USP-50-dependent regulation and suppresses both enlarged EE and diminished LE phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C56 are well-supported by microscopy and line scan analysis (Figure 5E-I) showing that K88R behaves like wild-type RABX-5 while K323R is insensitive to usp-50 mutation, and genetic suppression experiments (Figure 5J-M) demonstrating that K323R rescues both EE and LE phenotypes. The site-specific mutagenesis provides strong evidence for K323 as the critical regulatory site.

results.result: USP-50/USP8 is recruited to early endosomes by RABX-5/Rabex5, where it deubiquitinates the Vps9 domain to dissociate RABX-5 from endosomes while promoting SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 recruitment, thereby facilitating endosome maturation.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C58 and C73-C75 (and C83-C85 from abstract) represent the central mechanistic model supported by multiple lines of evidence: USP-50 localization depends on RABX-5 (C34), K323 deubiquitination is critical (C56), SAND-1/Mon1 recruitment is impaired in usp-50 mutants (C61, C64-C65), and the phenotypes are consistent with impaired endosome maturation (C1, C9, C67-C68). The comprehensive genetic, biochemical, and cell biological data strongly support this model.

results.result: GFP::SAND-1 puncta and LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosomes are diminished in both rabx-5(null) and usp-50 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C61 are supported by microscopy images and line scan analysis (Figure 6A-D) and quantification (Figure 6E-F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) showing reduced SAND-1 and lysosome signals in both mutants. The similar phenotypes suggest a pathway relationship.

results.result: In mammalian cells, Mon1a localizes to both early and late endosomes while Mon1b is more restricted to late endosomes, and USP8 knockdown reduces both Mon1a and Mon1b vesicle numbers, demonstrating evolutionary conservation.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C66 are supported by co-localization microscopy (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B-G) showing differential localization of Mon1a and Mon1b, and quantification (Figure 6H-I) showing reduced Mon1-positive vesicles upon USP8 knockdown. The conservation across species strengthens the findings.

results.result: sand-1 mutants phenocopy usp-50 mutants with enlarged early endosomes and smaller late endosomes/lysosomes, and USP-50 can bind to SAND-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C69 are supported by microscopy and quantification (Figure 6J-O, Figure 6—figure supplement 1H-I) showing similar phenotypes in sand-1 and usp-50 mutants, and co-immunoprecipitation (Figure 6P) demonstrating direct interaction. The phenotypic similarity and physical interaction support a functional relationship.

results.result: RAB-7 signal is reduced in both sand-1 and usp-50 mutants, and overexpression of rab-7 suppresses the enlarged early endosome phenotype of usp-50 mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C72 are supported by microscopy and line scan analysis (Figure 6Q-T) showing reduced RAB-7 signal in mutants, and rescue experiments (Figure 6U-X) demonstrating that rab-7 overexpression suppresses the EE enlargement phenotype. The genetic suppression provides strong evidence that reduced Rab7 contributes to the usp-50 phenotype.

results.result: The aberrantly enlarged vesicles in usp-50/USP8 mutants likely represent excessively enlarged early endosomes with abundant intraluminal vesicles.
results.evaluation: Claims C79 and C88 are inferred from multiple observations: reduced Rab7 levels (C71, C87), reduced lysosomes (C1, C89), enlarged FYVE-positive vesicles (C9), and EM showing ILV-containing vesicles (C16-C20). While the interpretation is reasonable given the data, the identity of these vesicles as arrested early endosomes versus aberrant MVBs could benefit from additional markers.

results.result: In USP8-deficient cells, active Rab5 levels are increased while Rab7 signal is decreased, resulting in rudimentary digestive lysosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C87 and C89 summarize key findings supported by pull-down assays (C44), microscopy (C42-C43, C71), and lysosome quantification (C1). These represent the major phenotypic consequences of USP8 loss.

results.result: The function of USP-50/USP8 in regulating endosome maturation is evolutionarily conserved between C. elegans and mammals.
results.evaluation: Claims C14 and C66 are supported by cross-species rescue experiments (C12-C13), similar phenotypes in mammalian cells (C15, C39, C46), and conserved effects on Mon1/SAND-1 localization (C64-C65). The multiple lines of evidence across species provide strong support for functional conservation.

results.result: USP8 plays important roles in ESCRT component stability, endosomal sorting of transmembrane receptors, and is a promising therapeutic target in cancer and Cushing's disease, though its effects on protein stability are variable.
results.evaluation: Claims C76 and C80-C107 are supported by citations to extensive prior literature. These claims provide important context for the current work but represent established knowledge rather than new findings from this study.

results.result: Background on endosome maturation: Rab5-to-Rab7 transition is crucial for endosome maturation, involving Rabex5-mediated Rab5 activation, Rabaptin-5-dependent positive feedback, and Mon1-Ccz1-mediated Rab7 activation and Rabex5 dissociation.
results.evaluation: Claims C82 and C90-C101 provide essential background on endosome maturation mechanisms, supported by citations to prior literature. These establish the context for understanding the novel findings about USP8's role.

results.result: Loss of USP-50/USP8 function leads to reduced lysosome size and volume in both C. elegans and mammalian cells. In C. elegans, usp-50(xd413) mutants show greatly reduced lysosome size, while usp-50(gk632973) animals display normal lysosomes at L4 stage but reduced size at adult stage. Similarly, late endosomes/lysosomes become smaller in sand-1 mutants, and digestive lysosomes are rudimentary in USP8-deficient mammalian cells.
results.evaluation: All reviewers acknowledge the reduced lysosome phenotype as a key finding. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'employed confocal imaging to obtain a picture of the aftermath of USP-50 loss' showing 'enlarged early endosomes and MVB-like structures' alongside reduced lysosomes. Reviewer 2 confirms 'the late endosomes and lysosomal compartments are reduced' in USP8 mutant cells. No reviewer challenges these observations.

results.result: NUC-1 protein is properly targeted to LAAT-1-containing vesicles in usp-50(xd413) animals, indicating that de novo lysosome assembly is not affected by usp-50 mutation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question this finding. The claim addresses a potential alternative explanation (defective lysosome assembly) and rules it out, which supports the authors' focus on endosome maturation defects. No reviewer raises concerns about this control experiment.

results.result: The punctate HGRS-1::GFP and STAM-1 signals (ESCRT-0 components) are greatly reduced in usp-50 mutants, consistent with USP8's known role in stabilizing the ESCRT-0 complex.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as consistent with established USP8 function. Reviewer 2 notes the work 'expands the targets and modes of action of USP8' without challenging the ESCRT-0 observations. The finding aligns with cited literature and is not disputed.

results.result: Early endosomes are significantly enlarged in usp-50/USP8 mutants across both C. elegans and mammalian cells. Individual early endosome size increases while total volume remains similar to wild-type, suggesting increased homotypic fusion. The enlarged early endosomes are not coated with lysosome markers and contain abundant intraluminal vesicles.
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a major finding. Reviewer 1 states 'Their findings indicated enlarged early endosomes and MVB-like structures in cells deficient in USP-50/USP8.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the early endosomes and MVB-like structures are enlarged.' Reviewer 3 notes 'an increased number of abnormal enlarged vesicles (aberrant early endosomes).' The evidence from both model systems is accepted.

results.result: The enlarged early endosome defect in usp-50(xd413) mutants is rescued by either worm usp-50 or human USP8, demonstrating evolutionary conservation of USP-50/USP8 function.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the evolutionary conservation. Reviewer 3 specifically highlights as a strength 'The use of two models, C. elegans and a mammalian cell line to describe a similar mechanism.' The cross-species rescue experiments are not questioned and support the generalizability of findings.

results.result: Transmission electron microscopy reveals many abnormal large vesicles with various intraluminal contents in usp-50(xd413) mutants, classified into four types: vesicles with abundant intraluminal vesicles (58.7%), threadlike membrane structures (26.8%), threadlike membranes with electron-dense material (22.4%), and vesicles containing organelles like mitochondria (4.9%).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly identifies this as a weakness: 'there is a need for further investigation to accurately characterize the anomalous structures detected in the ups-50 mutant. Also, the correlation between the presence of these abnormal structures and ESCRT-0 is yet to be addressed, and the current working model needs to be revised to prevent any confusion between enlarged early endosomes and MVBs.' This indicates the reviewers find the characterization incomplete.

results.result: USP-50/USP8 localizes specifically to early endosomes (co-localizing with RAB-5/Rab5 and EEA1) but not late endosomes (RAB-7/Rab7a) or lysosomes. USP8 forms individual spots at subdomains of early endosomes and is recruited to nascent Rab5-positive vesicles.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the localization data. Reviewer 2 notes 'The high-quality images provide clear in vivo evidences to support the main conclusions.' The subcellular localization is consistent with the proposed mechanism and is not challenged.

results.result: The early endosome localization of USP-50 is not dependent on its deubiquitination activity, as the catalytically inactive USP-50(C492A) mutant still co-localizes with RAB-5. However, overexpression of USP-50(C492A) has a dominant-negative effect, enhancing the RAB-5 signal.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these findings. The data support the distinction between USP-50 localization (independent of catalytic activity) and function (dependent on catalytic activity), which is important for the mechanistic model.

results.result: USP-50 binds to RABX-5 (Rabex5) through multiple domains, with the C-terminal coiled-coil and proline-rich domains being sufficient for interaction. The N-terminal region can also mediate binding, and including the Vps9 domain enhances the interaction. RABX-5 is required for the endosomal localization of USP-50.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the USP8-Rabex5 interaction as a key finding. Reviewer 2 states 'The work identifies a fascinating link between USP8 and the Rab5 guanine nucleotide exchange factor Rabx5, which expands the targets and modes of action of USP8.' The binding studies and localization dependency are not challenged.

results.result: In rabx-5(null) mutant animals, early endosomes appear normal, but the rabx-5(null) mutation suppresses the enlarged early endosome phenotype of usp-50(xd413), suggesting USP-50 exerts its regulatory effects on early endosome size through RABX-5.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 initially noted as a weakness: 'the authors didn't confirm whether and/or to which extent that USP8 regulates endosome maturation through Rabx5. Additional genetic and molecular evidence might be required to better support their working model.' However, the reviewer adds 'Note that the authors have provided convincing evidence about the role of USP8-Rabx5 axis in the revised manuscript,' suggesting this was addressed in revision but leaving some uncertainty about the initial submission.

results.result: RABX-5/Rabex5 signal is greatly enhanced and accumulates on enlarged endosomes in usp-50/USP8 mutants. In mammalian cells, USP8-KO causes increased numbers of enlarged endosomes with enriched Rabex5 that co-localizes with Rab5c and EEA1.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this as evidence for the mechanism. Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'show that USP8 likely targets specific lysine residue of Rabx5 to dissociate it from early endosomes,' indicating acceptance of the Rabex5 accumulation data as supporting the model.

results.result: In usp-50 mutants, GFP::RAB-5-labeled vesicles are significantly enlarged, the proportion of membrane-associated RAB-5 is increased, and there is more activated RAB-5 in vivo. Total RAB-5 protein levels are also increased. Similar enlargement of Rab5-labeled early endosomes occurs in USP8-KD mammalian cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 initially raised as a weakness: 'The authors utilized multiple fluorescent protein reporters...these results cannot tell that whether the endogenous proteins (Rab5, Rabex5, Rab7, etc.) are affected in the same fashion.' However, the reviewer adds 'Note that the authors have provided convincing evidence about the effects on Rab proteins in the revised manuscript,' suggesting concerns were addressed but indicating initial uncertainty.

results.result: USP-50/USP8 recruitment dissociates RABX-5 from endosomes through its deubiquitination activity, as the catalytically inactive USP-50(C492A) cannot rescue the enhanced endosomal RABX-5 signal in usp-50 mutants.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this mechanistic conclusion. Reviewer 1 states 'The results support their conclusions that UPS-50 acts by disassociating RABX-5 from early endosomes to deactivate RAB-5.' The requirement for catalytic activity is demonstrated and not disputed.

results.result: K88 and K323 residues of RABX-5 are ubiquitinated in vivo. K323, located in the Vps9 domain, is critical for USP-50 regulation: the K323R mutation prevents USP-50 from regulating RABX-5 endosomal localization and suppresses both the enlarged early endosome and diminished late endosome phenotypes of usp-50 mutants. K88R mutation does not prevent regulation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the identification of K323 as the critical ubiquitination site. Reviewer 2 states the authors 'show that USP8 likely targets specific lysine residue of Rabx5 to dissociate it from early endosomes,' indicating acceptance of this molecular detail. The genetic suppression by K323R is strong evidence.

results.result: The authors propose a model where USP-50/USP8 recruitment to early endosomes relies on RABX-5, and through deubiquitination of the Vps9 domain (K323), USP-50 dissociates RABX-5 from early endosomes, terminating Rab5 signaling. Concurrently, this promotes recruitment of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1, facilitating endosome maturation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the overall model. Reviewer 1 states 'The results support their conclusions that UPS-50 acts by disassociating RABX-5 from early endosomes to deactivate RAB-5 and by recruiting SAND-1/Mon1 to activate RAB-7.' The editor notes 'the dual actions of UPS-50 and USP8 in the conversion of early endosomes into late endosomes' are well-supported. The model integrates multiple lines of evidence accepted by reviewers.

results.result: GFP::SAND-1 puncta and LAAT-1::GFP-labeled lysosomes are diminished in rabx-5(null) mutants, and the punctate distribution of GFP::SAND-1 is lost in usp-50 mutants. Similarly, in mammalian cells, USP8 knockdown greatly reduces the number of vesicles positive for Mon1a or Mon1b. This indicates the function of USP8/USP-50 in endosomal localization of SAND-1/Mon1-Ccz1 is evolutionarily conserved.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the SAND-1/Mon1 recruitment defect as part of the mechanism. Reviewer 1 states the results support 'recruiting SAND-1/Mon1 to activate RAB-7.' The evolutionary conservation across worms and mammalian cells strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: In mammalian SUM159 cells, mEGFP-tagged endogenous Mon1a localizes to both Rab5-positive early endosomes and Rab7-positive late endosomes, while Mon1b is more localized to late endosomes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this characterization of Mon1a/b localization in mammalian cells. It provides context for understanding the Mon1 complex function and is consistent with the overall model.

results.result: sand-1 mutants phenocopy usp-50 mutants with enlarged early endosomes and smaller late endosomes/lysosomes. USP-50 protein binds to SAND-1, consistent with USP-50's role in SAND-1 endosomal localization.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the sand-1 mutant phenotype and USP-50/SAND-1 interaction as supporting the model. The phenotypic similarity between sand-1 and usp-50 mutants strengthens the conclusion that USP-50 acts through SAND-1 recruitment.

results.result: The punctate RAB-7 signal is greatly reduced in both sand-1 and usp-50 mutants. Overexpression of wild-type rab-7 suppresses the early endosome enlargement phenotype of usp-50 mutants. In USP8-deficient mammalian cells, the Rab7 signal is decreased.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the reduced Rab7 as a consequence of impaired endosome maturation. Reviewer 2 states 'the late endosomes and lysosomal compartments are reduced' in USP8 mutants. The rab-7 overexpression rescue provides functional evidence that reduced Rab7 contributes to the phenotype.

results.result: Loss of USP-50 results in upregulation of Rab5 signaling, which may enhance homophilic fusion of early endosomes. The aberrantly enlarged vesicles in usp-50 mutants likely represent excessively enlarged early endosomes rather than MVBs. In USP8-deficient cells, the level of active Rab5 is increased.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 specifically identifies this as needing clarification: 'the current working model needs to be revised to prevent any confusion between enlarged early endosomes and MVBs.' The interpretation of the abnormal structures as enlarged early endosomes versus MVBs remains a point of uncertainty requiring further investigation.

comparisons.comparison: Both support reduced lysosome phenotype (C1, C2). OpenEval emphasizes microscopy evidence and temporal differences between alleles. Peer review groups this with other claims (C60, C68, C89) as key findings. Both find evidence convincing.

Both support C3 (no defect in lysosome biogenesis). OpenEval notes proper NUC-1/LAAT-1 co-localization. Peer review accepts this control experiment without challenge, supporting focus on endosome maturation defects.

Perfect agreement on C7-C8 (reduced ESCRT-0 signals). Both find evidence supported by microscopy and consistent with established USP8 function in ESCRT-0 stabilization. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both support enlarged early endosomes (C9-C11). OpenEval cites quantification showing increased individual EE size. Peer review explicitly acknowledges this as major finding across all three reviewers, with evidence from both C. elegans and mammalian cells (C15, C42, C46, C67, C88).
Perfect agreement on cross-species rescue (C12-C14). Both evaluations support functional conservation between worm and human orthologs. Peer review highlights use of two model systems as a strength.
Both address enlarged endosomes in mammalian cells (C15). OpenEval finds evidence supported. Peer review accepts this as part of the major finding of enlarged early endosomes across species.

Divergent evaluations of ultrastructural characterization (C16-C20, C77). OpenEval finds EM evidence strongly supports abnormal vesicle categories with specific percentages. Peer review (Reviewer 1) finds characterization incomplete and requests further investigation to distinguish enlarged early endosomes from MVBs.

Both support USP-50 early endosome localization (C21-C22). OpenEval emphasizes co-localization with RAB-5 but not RAB-7. Peer review accepts localization data (C25-C29) as consistent with proposed mechanism, noting high-quality images.

Both address catalytically inactive mutant (C23-C24). OpenEval finds C23 supported but C24 uncertain, noting limited evidence for dominant-negative mechanism. Peer review accepts these findings as supporting distinction between localization and function.
Both support USP8 localization to early endosomes in mammalian cells (C25-C26). OpenEval cites co-localization with EEA1. Peer review accepts this as part of comprehensive localization data.

Both support dynamic USP8 localization (C27-C29). OpenEval emphasizes multi-modal imaging showing asymmetric distribution and dynamic recruitment. Peer review accepts these observations as part of high-quality imaging evidence.

Both support USP8-Rabex5 interaction and domain mapping (C30-C34). OpenEval finds co-IP and domain analysis provide clear evidence. Peer review identifies this as a key finding expanding USP8 targets and modes of action.

Both address genetic epistasis (C34-C37). OpenEval finds strong support from loss of USP-50 localization and phenotype suppression in rabx-5(null). Peer review initially noted weakness requiring additional evidence but indicates concerns were addressed in revision.
Perfect agreement on enhanced Rabex5 signal (C38-C41). Both find evidence supported by microscopy and quantification in both model systems. Conservation across species strengthens findings.

Both address upregulated Rab5 signaling (C42-C46, C78). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence from multiple assays strongly supportive. Peer review initially raised concerns about fluorescent reporters vs endogenous proteins but indicates concerns were addressed in revision.
Perfect agreement on catalytic activity requirement (C47-C49). Both find failure of C492A mutant to rescue provides strong evidence for deubiquitination-dependent mechanism.
Both support identification of ubiquitination sites (C50-C52). OpenEval cites mass spectrometry data. Peer review accepts these findings as part of identifying K323 as critical site.

Both strongly support K323 as critical regulatory site (C53-C56). OpenEval emphasizes site-specific mutagenesis and genetic suppression. Peer review accepts K323R data showing USP8 targets specific lysine to dissociate Rabex5.

Both support overall mechanistic model (C57-C58, C73-C75, C83-C85). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence strongly supports dual action model. Peer review accepts model of USP-50 dissociating RABX-5 and recruiting SAND-1/Mon1, with editor noting dual actions are well-supported.

Both support reduced SAND-1/Mon1 and lysosome signals (C59-C61). OpenEval cites microscopy and quantification. Peer review accepts this as part of mechanism involving SAND-1/Mon1 recruitment defect (also C64-C66).
Both support Mon1a/b differential localization (C62-C63). OpenEval emphasizes conservation across species. Peer review accepts characterization without challenge as consistent with overall model.

Both support impaired Mon1/SAND-1 recruitment (C64-C66). OpenEval cites reduced Mon1-positive vesicles upon USP8 knockdown. Peer review accepts this as part of mechanism with evolutionary conservation strengthening conclusion.
Perfect agreement on sand-1 mutant phenotype and USP-50/SAND-1 interaction (C67-C69). Both find phenotypic similarity and physical interaction support functional relationship in the pathway.

Both support reduced Rab7 and genetic suppression by rab-7 overexpression (C70-C72, C87). OpenEval emphasizes genetic suppression as strong evidence. Peer review accepts reduced Rab7 as consequence of impaired endosome maturation.

Divergent evaluations of vesicle identity (C79, C88). OpenEval finds interpretation reasonable but notes identity as arrested early endosomes vs aberrant MVBs could benefit from additional markers. Peer review (Reviewer 1) explicitly requests clarification to prevent confusion between enlarged early endosomes and MVBs.

Both support major phenotypic consequences (C86-C87, C89). OpenEval summarizes key findings from pull-down assays and microscopy. Peer review groups these with reduced lysosome phenotype as key findings.
Both support functional conservation across species (C14, C66). OpenEval cites cross-species rescue and conserved effects on Mon1/SAND-1. Peer review highlights use of two model systems as strength.
